name: subsidence
job: Forecast how far each spot will have sunk at the next NISAR Pass, with an uncertainty, and flag statistically significant accelerating ground
user: City water and infrastructure planners watching where the ground sinks fastest

labels.source: The site's own NISAR GUNW NSBAS series; Passes 2026-10-01, 2026-10-01, 2026-10-13 held out
labels.notes: Scores measure forecasts of the next Passes, not levelling or GNSS truth; the atmosphere of a future Pass is an irreducible error floor

baseline.name: Straight-line extrapolation of each pixel's history

model.name: LightGBM quantile (selected on a validation origin)

split: Time split: test = last 3 Passes (origin 2026-09-19); model chosen on validation origin 2026-09-07; learned models trained on rolling origins with targets before each origin
limits: Does not significantly beat the straight-line Baseline: use the Baseline; the Model is shown for transparency
About one year of NISAR data: seasonal terms are only marginally resolved
Line-of-sight displacement; vertical motion assumed when converting with the incidence angle
Forecasts cannot anticipate changes in pumping policy or recharge
PROVISIONAL products; the LOS sign is the ISCE convention, checked here against the sinking lake-bed
